name: CLIProxyAPI
description: Runs CLIProxyAPI on this machine and routes Claude and Codex through it, so your agents use the accounts you sign in to there: several Claude or Codex subscriptions taking turns, or API keys of your own. Adds "Claude via CLIProxyAPI" and "Codex via CLIProxyAPI" to Settings → Providers and keeps them pointed at the proxy. Its page signs accounts in, shows what each account and model used, the proxy's log, and the upstream API keys.

permissions.reason: To add "Claude via CLIProxyAPI" and "Codex via CLIProxyAPI" to Settings → Providers and keep their address and key in step with the proxy. Rename, switch off or delete them like your own; one you delete stays deleted until you add it back from the plugin's page.

settings.label: Proxy

options.label: Connect to a CLIProxyAPI already running

settings.description: Run starts the proxy with the MC and stops it with the plugin. Connect uses one you run yourself, at the address and with the management key below.

settings.label: cli-proxy-api binary
settings.description: Left empty, the plugin uses cli-proxy-api from PATH, or else downloads CLIProxyAPI 8.0.79 for this machine from its GitHub release, checked against the release's checksums.

settings.label: Port
settings.description: The port the proxy listens on, on 127.0.0.1 only.

settings.label: Address to connect to
settings.description: With Connect: the proxy's address as this machine reaches it, such as http://127.0.0.1:8317.

settings.label: Management key
settings.description: With Connect: the proxy's management key (remote-management.secret-key). Run makes its own.
